lessons.title: From Egg to Chick
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe that a chick hatches from an egg.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a real or picture egg and discuss what might be inside.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce the concept that a chick grows inside an egg and hatches out, using picture sequence cards.

differentiation.extension: Explain the process in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of life cycles — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Talk about eggs and where they come from with family.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Chick's Story' or 'Little Chick'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence the chick's journey from egg to hatching.
lessons.main_activity: Read a simple chick life-cycle story, pausing to discuss each stage.
key_questions: What does the chick do to get out of the egg?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of sequence — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Counting Eggs in a Nest
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count eggs accurately up to 10.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a nest of egg pictures together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count and place a given number of egg counters into nest templates, checking accuracy.
key_questions: How many eggs are in this nest?
Can you count them again to check?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.home_link: Count eggs or small objects at home together.

lessons.title: What Do Chicks Need to Grow?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a baby chick needs to grow healthy.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what a plant needs to grow (Week 5).
lessons.main_activity: Discuss what a chick needs (warmth from the mother hen, food, water, safety) using pictures.
key_questions: What does a chick need to grow?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of animal care needs — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what chicks need to grow.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what a pet or baby animal needs to grow.

lessons.title: Writing Life Cycle Labels
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple label for each life cycle stage.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw the life cycle stages (egg, chick, hen) and attempt to write a label for each using known phonics sounds.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress and sequencing understanding — evidence for LIT.3/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled life cycle drawings with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw and label a life cycle together at home.

lessons.title: Ordering the Life Cycle Stages
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order the life cycle stages using ordinal numbers.
lessons.main_activity: Children order life cycle picture cards (egg, chick, hen) using ordinal number labels.
resources_needed: Life cycle sequencing cards, ordinal number labels
key_questions: What comes first in the life cycle?

differentiation.extension: Use ordinal language independently for all stages

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ordinal number and sequencing understanding — evidence for MATHS.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of the life cycle order using ordinal numbers.
lessons.home_link: Practise ordinal numbers with a simple sequence at home.

lessons.title: Other Animals That Hatch from Eggs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name another animal that hatches from an egg.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap that chicks hatch from eggs.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss other egg-laying animals (frogs, turtles, butterflies, other birds) using picture cards, sorting egg-layers vs non-egg-layers.
key_questions: What other animals hatch from eggs?
How many egg-laying animals can you find?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note broadened understanding of life cycles — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look up another animal that hatches from an egg together.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Life Cycle Stories
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a similarity between two life cycle stories.
lessons.main_activity: Read/discuss a second life-cycle themed story (e.g. about a frog or butterfly) and compare life cycle stages.
key_questions: What is similar about these life cycles?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative reasoning across scientific topics — evidence for LIT.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of similarities and differences found.
lessons.home_link: Compare two animal life cycles you know about at home.

lessons.title: Number Bonds Recap: Egg Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall number bonds to 10 using an egg-themed activity.
lessons.main_activity: Using egg counters split between two nests, children practise and record all number bonds to 10.
key_questions: What are all the ways to make 10?
Can you recall this without counting?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess number bond to 10 fluency — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all bonds to 10.
lessons.home_link: Practise number bonds to 10 with any small objects at home.

lessons.title: Observing Real Eggs (If Available) or Video Resources
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make an observation about a real or filmed egg/chick.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the life cycle learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: (If class has real eggs incubating) observe and discuss; otherwise watch a short age-appropriate video of chicks hatching and discuss observations.
resources_needed: Real eggs/incubator or hatching video resource
key_questions: How does the chick get out of the egg?

differentiation.support: Watch and describe with adult prompts
differentiation.extension: Describe the process in detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and scientific language — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Watch a nature video about baby animals together if possible.

lessons.title: Retelling the Life Cycle Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the full chick life cycle using sequencing vocabulary.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the life cycle stages using picture cards.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children retell the full life cycle (egg, chick, hen, laying eggs again) using a circular life cycle diagram.
key_questions: What happens after the chick grows into a hen?

differentiation.support: Retell with adult prompting at each stage
differentiation.extension: Explain that the cycle repeats independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of cyclical processes — evidence for LIT.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: One pair retells the full cycle to the class.
lessons.home_link: Explain the life cycle to your family using the diagram.

lessons.title: Sorting Eggs by Size
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sort and order eggs by size.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at pictures of different egg sizes (quail, hen, ostrich).
lessons.main_activity: Children sort and order egg picture cutouts from smallest to biggest, discussing size differences.
resources_needed: Egg picture cutouts of varying sizes
lessons.assessment_notes: Note size-ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of egg size order.
lessons.home_link: Compare sizes of eggs or other round objects at home.

lessons.title: Life Cycles Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about life cycles learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Life Cycles' display summarising the chick life cycle and other egg-laying animals.
key_questions: What have we learned about life cycles?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about life cycles with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Life Cycle Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple life-cycle themed words.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading life-cycle themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'the hen has an egg').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading life cycle words over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Ordinals, Number Bonds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, ordinal numbers, and number bonds to 10 skills from this week.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting eggs, ordinal life cycle sequencing, number bonds to 10.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and ordering over the weekend.
